questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. I was completely mesmerised by the performance.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
I was completely mesmerised by the performance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fascinated.

Key Points

  • The word "mesmerised" means to hold the attention of someone to the exclusion of all else or so as to transfix them. (मंत्रमुग्ध)
    • Example: The magician's performance left the audience mesmerised.
  • "Fascinated" refers to being intensely interested in or attracted by someone or something. (मोहित)
    • Example: She was fascinated by the intricate details of the painting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fascinated.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Irritated (चिढ़): Feeling annoyed or slightly angry.
    • Example: She was irritated by the constant noise outside her window.
  • Annoyed (परेशान): Slightly angry; irritated.
    • Example: He was annoyed by the delay in the delivery of his package.
  • Bored (उबाऊ): Feeling weary and impatient because one is unoccupied or lacks interest in one's current activity.
    • Example: The lecture was so dull that the students appeared bored.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Easy does it
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Easy does it

options.text: Used to tell someone to do something rarely
options.html: Used to tell someone to do something rarely

options.text: Used to tell someone to do something violently
options.html: Used to tell someone to do something violently

options.text: Used to tell someone to do something slowly and carefully
options.html: Used to tell someone to do something slowly and carefully

options.text: Used to tell someone to do something horridly
options.html: Used to tell someone to do something horridly

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Easy does it" means to do something slowly and carefully. (धीरे और सावधानी से कुछ करना)
    • Example: When lifting heavy objects, remember, easy does it to avoid injury.
  • "Easy does it" advises caution and a measured approach. (सावधानी और मापी हुई पद्धति की सलाह देना)
    • Example: While painting the delicate artwork, easy does it to ensure precision.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: Used to tell someone to do something rarely (किसी को कुछ कम बार करने के लिए कहना)
    • Example: You should eat junk food rarely to maintain good health.
  • Option 2: Used to tell someone to do something violently (किसी को कुछ हिंसक रूप से करने के लिए कहना)
    • Example: He was told to act violently in the action scene of the movie.
  • Option 4: Used to tell someone to do something horridly (किसी को कुछ भयानक तरीके से करने के लिए कहना)
    • Example: The villain in the story was asked to act horridly to frighten the audience.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Candid
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Candid
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Dishonest.

Key Points

  • The word "candid" means being straightforward, honest, and open in speech or expression. (स्पष्टवादी)
    • Example: She gave a candid interview about her experiences in the industry.
  • "Dishonest" refers to someone who is not honest, who lies or cheats. (बेईमान)
    • Example: His dishonest behavior led to a loss of trust among his colleagues.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'candid' is 'dishonest'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Dishonest.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Tender (कोमल): Showing gentleness and concern or sympathy.
    • Example: She touched the injured bird with tender care.
  • Guileless (निर्दोष): Innocent and without deception.
    • Example: His guileless smile won everyone's heart.
  • Irrelevant (अप्रासंगिक): Not connected with or relevant to something.
    • Example: His comments were completely irrelevant to the discussion.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Educational technology has become a necesity if one desires excellent output.
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:

Key Points

The misspelled word is 'necesity'.

  • The correct spelling would be 'necessity'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cut corners
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Cut corners

options.text: Do something in an inexpensive and easy way
options.html: Do something in an inexpensive and easy way

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Do something in an inexpensive and easy way.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Cut corners" means to do something in the easiest, cheapest, or fastest way. (किसी काम को आसान, सस्ता, या सबसे तेज़ तरीके से करना)
    • Example: The contractor cut corners by using low-quality materials, which caused the building to collapse.
  • "Cut corners" refers to avoiding steps that are necessary or skipping important details to save time or money. (समय या पैसे बचाने के लिए आवश्यक कामों को छोड़ना)
    • Example: When you cut corners on safety, you put everyone at risk.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Do something in an inexpensive and easy way.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Complete a work (काम पूरा करना): To finish a task or project.
    • Example: She managed to complete the work before the deadline.
  • Find a suitable place (उचित स्थान खोजें): To locate an appropriate location for something.
    • Example: They need to find a suitable place for the new office.
  • Clear a space (जगह साफ़ करना): To remove obstacles or clutter from an area.
    • Example: We need to clear a space in the garage for the new car.

questions.question: Identify the error in the following sentence. Brr, the city view from the Eiffel Tower is amazing!
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the error in the following sentence.
Brr, the city view from the Eiffel Tower is amazing!
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

Key Points

The error in the sentence is the use of the interjection 'Brr' which is not appropriate in this context.

  • 'Brr' is typically used to indicate that someone is cold, which doesn't fit the context of admiring a city view.
  • The correct way to express this sentence would be to simply start with 'The city view from the Eiffel Tower is amazing!'
  • Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Additional Information

Let's understand the other options - 

  • Option 1: 'amazing' -  This word is correctly used to describe the view.
  • Option 2: 'from' -  This word is correctly used to indicate the origin of the view.
  • Option 3: 'view' -  This word is correctly used to refer to what is seen from the Eiffel Tower.

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A thing fit to eat.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A thing fit to eat.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1'.

Key Points

  • The word "Edible" (Option 1) refers to something that is fit to be eaten, which directly matches the meaning of the given phrase.
  • Options 2 ("Unpalatable"), 3 ("Uneatable"), and 4 ("Toxic") refer to things that are not suitable to eat, making them incorrect choices.

Hence, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.

Explanation: The term "Edible" best fits the definition of "a thing fit to eat." It refers to something that is safe and suitable for consumption.

Additional Information

  • Option 2: "Unpalatable" means not pleasant to taste, which contradicts the idea of something being fit to eat.
  • Option 3: "Uneatable" suggests something that cannot be eaten, which does not match the given phrase.
  • Option 4: "Toxic" refers to something harmful or poisonous, which is the opposite of being fit to eat.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Reluctant
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Reluctant
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Enthusiastic.

Key Points

  • The word "Reluctant" means unwilling and hesitant; disinclined. (अनिच्छुक)
    • Example: She was reluctant to join the meeting because she was not prepared.
  • "Enthusiastic" refers to showing intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval. (उत्साही)
    • Example: He was enthusiastic about starting his new job next week.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Reluctant' is 'Enthusiastic'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Enthusiastic.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Desperate (बेकरार): Desperate means feeling a strong need or urgency, often because of hopelessness or distress.
    It expresses emotional intensity or anxious urgency, not willingness.
    • Example: She was desperate to find a job after months of unemployment.
  • Obedient (आज्ञाकारी): Obedient means following orders, not necessarily willingly. 
    • Example: The obedient dog followed all the commands of its owner.
  • Beautiful (सुंदर): Pleasing the senses or mind aesthetically.
    • Example: The beautiful sunset left everyone in awe.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'. If it had not rained, they would not postpone the programmes.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'.
If it had not rained, they would not postpone the programmes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence is in the past perfect conditional form.
  • The correct structure for such sentences is: If + past perfect, would + have + past participle.
  • The correct phrase should be "would not have postponed," ensuring grammatical correctness.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "If it had not rained, they would not have postponed the programmes."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "would be postponed" – This option is incorrect because it does not match the past perfect conditional structure.
  • Option 2: "no substitution" – This option is incorrect because the original sentence is not grammatically correct.
  • Option 4: "would not postponed" – This option is incorrect because it is not grammatically correct; "postponed" should be in the past participle form.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Having known that / the train was already on the platform, / they ran fastly / to catch it.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Having known that / the train was already on the platform, / they ran fastly / to catch it.

options.text: the train was already on the platform
options.html: the train was already on the platform

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the word "fastly" instead of the correct adverb "fast."
  • The word "fastly" is not a proper word in English. The correct adverb form of "fast" is simply "fast."
  • The correct phrase should be "they ran fast," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in part 1 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "Having known that the train was already on the platform, they ran fast to catch it."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. The movie's plot was predictable , with clichéd twists and turns.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence.
The movie's plot was predictable, with clichéd twists and turns.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The word "predictable" means something that can be anticipated or expected beforehand; it refers to events or situations that unfold in a manner consistent with what is generally foreseen. (पूर्वानुमेय)
    • Example: The outcome of the election was predictable, given the current political climate.
  • "Unexpected" refers to something that is not anticipated or foreseen; it happens suddenly without prior indication. (अप्रत्याशित)
    • Example: The sudden rainstorm was completely unexpected and caught everyone by surprise.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'predictable' is 'unexpected'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Undeviating (अविचलित): Not changing or swerving from a predetermined course.
    • Example: The pilot maintained an undeviating course throughout the flight.
  • Evident (स्पष्ट): Clearly seen or understood; obvious.
    • Example: The benefits of the new policy were evident to everyone.
  • Infelicitous (अप्रसन्न): Not suitable or appropriate; unfortunate.
    • Example: His infelicitous remark at the meeting caused discomfort among the attendees.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. By whom were you injured?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
By whom were you injured?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 (Who injured you?).  
The conversion is Passive to Active.  

Explanation: The original sentence is in Passive voice (Past Indefinite: "By whom were you injured?" - Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject). The correct answer converts this to Active voice in Past Indefinite (Subject + V2 + Object). Here, "Who" becomes the subject performing the action (injured), and "you" remains the object.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The patient was suffering from a chronic disease.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The patient was suffering from a chronic disease.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Mild.

Key Points

  • The word "chronic" means something persisting for a long time or constantly recurring, especially in the context of a disease. (दीर्घकालीन)
    • Example: He has been dealing with chronic back pain for years.
  • "Mild" refers to something not severe, serious, or harsh. It is gentle in effect or degree. (हल्का)
    • Example: He experienced mild symptoms of the flu, such as a slight fever and a sore throat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Mild.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Common (सामान्य): Occurring, found, or done often; prevalent.
    • Example: It is common for people to catch a cold during the winter months.
  • Universal (सार्वभौमिक): Applicable to all cases; existing or true at all times or in all places.
    • Example: The desire for love and acceptance is universal among humans.
  • Usual (सामान्य): Habitually or typically occurring or done; customary.
    • Example: She followed her usual routine of jogging and then having breakfast.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bold. Many people fought to abolish slavery during the Civil War.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bold.
Many people fought to abolish slavery during the Civil War.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. establish.

Key Points

  • The word "abolish" means to formally put an end to a system, practice, or institution. (समाप्त करना)
    • Example: The government decided to abolish the old tax laws to simplify the economic system.
  • "Establish" means to set up or create something, especially a system, practice, or institution. (स्थापित करना)
    • Example: The university plans to establish a new research center dedicated to advanced technologies.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'abolish' is 'establish'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. establish.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Kill (मार डालना): To cause the death of a living being.
    • Example: The hunter aimed to kill the deer with a single shot.
  • Terminate (समाप्त करना): To bring something to an end.
    • Example: The company decided to terminate the project due to budget constraints.
  • Damage (क्षति): Physical harm that impairs the value, usefulness, or normal function of something.
    • Example: The storm caused significant damage to the coastal areas.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Were the plants being grafted by the gardener?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Were the plants being grafted by the gardener?

options.text: Was the gardener grafting the plants?
options.html: Was the gardener grafting the plants?

options.text: Was the gardener grafted the plants?
options.html: Was the gardener grafted the plants?

options.text: Were the plants grafting the gardener?
options.html: Were the plants grafting the gardener?

options.text: Were the gardener grafting the plants?
options.html: Were the gardener grafting the plants?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the passive voice, the sentence is: "Were the plants being grafted by the gardener?"
  • To convert to active voice: Place the subject "the gardener" at the beginning.
  • Change the passive verb form "were being grafted" to "was grafting" (past continuous active).
  • Ensure the object "the plants" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "Was the gardener grafting the plants?"
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "Was the gardener grafted the plants?" – Incorrect as "grafted" is a past participle and does not form a valid sentence here.
  • Option 3: "Were the plants grafting the gardener?" – Incorrect as it reverses the subject and object.
  • Option 4: "Were the gardener grafting the plants?" – Incorrect due to subject-verb agreement ("were" does not match "the gardener").

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2

  • The word “committed” aligns with the idea of being openly dedicated or invested in expressing his opinions.
  • "Pacified", "sorted", and "isolated" do not fit the context of actively engaging or expressing strong feelings.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'frustrated'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage describes Rory Cooper’s feelings toward the lack of reopening of public schools in his area.
  • The appropriate word should reflect dissatisfaction and impatience caused by this situation.

questions.question: ​Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
